chunks: And from his words (peace be upon him), when he was criticized for making people equal in the distribution of gifts, without preference for the early comers and the nobles, he said:

key_terms.السَّبَاقَات: The early comers (those who embraced Islam early)

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Ali distribute wealth equally without favoring early Muslims or nobles?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) defended his policy of equal distribution (Sawa) from the Bayt al-Mal against critics who favored the early converts (Sabaqat) and nobles (Ashraf) based on merit or lineage. This decision reflected his commitment to egalitarian justice, prioritizing the principle of equal rights for all Muslims over hierarchical distinctions of seniority or social status. It underscores the Shia view that leadership should not confer automatic financial privilege, but rather serve the community with impartiality.
